results.headline: AGM Statement
results.key_quote: Fonix has made a positive start to the financial year and is trading in line with management expectations.
results.summary: Fonix reports a positive start to the financial year and explicitly states it is trading in line with management expectations. results.headline: Trading Update
results.key_quote: Profitability for FY26 remains in line with market expectations
results.summary: Marshalls reported ten-month revenue of £544 million in line with prior year on a like-for-like trading days basis. The company explicitly states that full year profitability remains in line with market expectations (analyst consensus of £49.7 million adjusted PBT with range £48.0-£50.6 million). While the company achieved market share gains and pricing actions in Landscaping, and modest growth in Roofing, these were offset by weakness in Building Products due to declining new housebuilding activity. Strong cash generation reduced net debt by £24 million year-on-year. The CEO commentary describes resilient but challenging trading with no upgrade to guidance.

results.key_quote: While operational momentum has improved, finance cost and FX have been adversely impacted by macroeconomic and political events in the period. As such, 2026 full year EPRA Earnings is expected to be in the range of 3.6 to 4.6 pence per share.
results.summary: CLS Holdings reports encouraging operational progress with strengthened leasing activity, improved underlying vacancy (excluding Spring Gardens departure), and strong October performance. However, this operational momentum is offset by adverse impacts from finance costs and FX headwinds due to macroeconomic and political events. The 2026 full year EPRA Earnings guidance of 3.6-4.6 pence per share reflects these offsetting factors. The company is on track with disposal targets and refinancing programmes. No explicit comparison to market or analyst expectations is provided, suggesting results are tracking in line with internal plans rather than materially ahead or behind external expectations.

results.headline: Bibemi Gold Project Update
results.key_quote: The key economic findings of the UFG Scoping Study for Bibemi are highly encouraging. Not only are there notable operational and potential financing benefits, but there is a large capital cost saving on the processing plant of US$13.7m, with only a slightly increased processing operating cost per ounce of gold produced.
results.summary: Oriole Resources announced a Scoping Study on an ultra-fine grinding (UFG) processing flowsheet for the Bibemi gold project, showing a 38% reduction in sulphide processing plant CAPEX (US$13.7m saving) and 23% reduction in total project CAPEX to US$46.7m. While the UFG method offers capital savings and operational simplicity benefits, the OPEX per ounce increased by 7.3% (US$42.4/oz increase) due to lower gold recovery (78.7% vs 85%), higher throughput processing costs, and increased power costs. The company characterizes findings as "highly encouraging" but provides no explicit comparison to prior market or analyst expectations. This represents a technical development with mixed economic trade-offs rather than a clear beat or miss versus expectations.
metrics_ahead: Capital cost reduction of 38% on processing plant
Total project CAPEX reduction of 23%
Operational simplicity improvements

No comparison to external expectations, board guidance, or analyst forecasts is provided.
